followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the formal Loyada asylum-admission/reception restriction, whose origin predates the observation window but is explicitly discussed in an October 2017 UNHCR submission. The evidence concerns asylum-seekers arriving from Somalia into Djibouti through the formal reception route. Informal arrivals continued. It does not establish closure to every traveller or all goods. Retain May 2014 month bounds, unknown endpoint and no day-specific last-confirmation date. The October 2017 document date stays in text, without inventing an observation day or a continuous numeric duration. No operational complete/exact flags or daily animation interval are created. The security/armed-attacks rationale follows UNHCR’s account of the May 2014 attack. An affected asylum cohort does not by itself support migration control as an additional official purpose. The UNHCR submission and its October date were freshly inspected. The 2014 UNHCR account remains a cached indexed extract, and both reports share the institutional origin. OSM records are coordinate evidence only. The approved approximate point matches saved OSM node 8405526244 at 11.4602871 / 43.2569738; nearby way 778712166 names the Djibouti–Somalia border post. This does not locate every informal route or prove historical operation. Policy-only display remains constrained by the lack of an in-window observation day.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the Moyale non-exempt passenger restriction and operational enforcement context; this is not evidence that all cargo stopped. The commissioner describes restricted persons in both directions, including informal-entry controls. Goods, a driver and turnboy remain excepted subject to health screening. The wider county frontier and informal routes are not all located. Retain the 24–29 March 2020 onset interval and 29 March last confirmation, with reopening unknown. The later trenches confrontation does not supply a reopening or establish continuous closure beyond the accepted confirmation. A zero-day lower bound is not a same-day completed closure. Human disease control follows the explicit COVID explanation. Trenching and illegal-entry language do not independently justify adding smuggling or migration purposes. The Standard passage was freshly retrieved; the Star passage and PIDA table were newly reread from saved receipts. The Star URL date differs from its displayed 1 April date, which is retained. No independent-origin count is inferred from the three source entries. The approved approximate Moyale point exactly matches PIDA E19, 3.52678 / 39.05284. It locates the named crossing component, not the reported county frontier or trench line. Preserve the qualified scope and stop animation at the last confirmation.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Deliberate truck obstruction of Kenya’s Malaba exit and approaches is supported. Ordinary congestion and queue clearance are not by themselves new closure episodes. The selected movement is cargo from Kenya toward Uganda. Pedestrians and boda bodas passed blocked approaches; reverse-direction trucks faced later queue-clearance timing. No all-passenger international closure is claimed. Reports support physical blockage on 21 May 2020 and scoped resumption around 15:00 on 26 May. The conflicting account of three days from Monday is real and remains unresolved. Later union advice to stop services is not an observed renewed blockade; numerical continuous duration remains withheld. Drivers stated health-protocol and treatment grievances. The minister’s alternative incitement account is retained as competing attribution, rather than replacing the protestors’ stated reason or being merged into a single proved cause. Five relevant article bodies were freshly checked, including the start, local endpoint, opposing continuity account, ministerial statement and passage exceptions. Original Star URLs redirect to changed categories; the historical articles remain readable. Earlier R01 challenge involvement is disclosed. The phase remains unlocated pending B01. The text distinguishes the Malaba exit from blocked approach roads; no precise blocked lane or whole border line is inferred.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the observed 23 March 2021 Busia freight protest, separate from the underlying maize commodity restriction. Traders and clearing agents obstructed trucks and customs documents in both directions. No universal passenger restriction is evidenced, and the movement obstruction is not represented as a state-ordered all-traffic closure. The Tuesday date supports 23 March onset and last confirmation. Several hours and later crisis meetings do not supply an observed reopening. Endpoint remains unknown; the zero-day lower bound is not a complete or exact operational duration. Trade and transport protest coding follows the participants’ complaints over maize restrictions, impounding and fines. The health reason for the underlying maize rule is not transferred to this protest as its rationale. The relevant Monitor paragraphs were freshly read before the registration wall. No inaccessible later content is recertified. The named reporter and the one source origin are retained; PIDA supplies geography only. PIDA E6 visually confirms 0.46555 / 34.09767 for the approved approximate Busia crossing marker. It is not the precise protest barricade or paperwork desk. followup_reviews.Research finding: Intentional Kenyan maize import holds are supported at two named crossings. These are distinct from a protest blockade and from Tanzania-bound transit-truck restrictions; retain the included parent. Busia concerns Ugandan maize awaiting Kenya entry. Namanga concerns Kenyan-owned maize from Tanzania; consignments returned to Tanzania are not Kenya-entry releases. Other goods and all-passenger closure are not claimed. P1 retains the dated Busia observation around 23 March 2021; P2 retains the 1 April Namanga spot check. Neither has a verified first denial or release. Do not backdate both to the reported 5 March policy or bridge the observations into a continuous all-frontier ban. Aflatoxin/mycotoxin concerns are the source-attributed food-safety justification. The later minister’s denial of a blanket ban and journalistic farmer/election context remain qualifications, not additional official rationales. Three relevant article bodies were freshly inspected. The Busia Monitor passage was available before a subscription prompt. Earlier challenge involvement is disclosed; fresh access does not create independent human review. Both accepted phases are unlocated pending B01. Named crossing identities support the textual scope, but no coordinates, gate line, or nationwide outline is certified here.

Indian pilgrimage groups travelling through Nathu La into China. Lipulekh remained a distinct operating pilgrimage route. No claim covers all cross-border trade or ordinary travel. P1 confirms cancellation as of 30 June 2017, without converting the scheduled 20 June trip into a first denied day. P2 retains actual first reported 2018 passage on 20 June. The annual June–September season prevents treating the intervening winter as continuous operational closure. The parliamentary answer reports China’s safe-conduct explanation. Keep the broad rationale uncoded rather than treating the military-standoff context as an independently established official interstate-pressure motive. The relevant parliamentary passages, cancellation dispatch, actual-passage report and seasonality answer were freshly read. PTI is the origin for two news articles; they concern different dated observations, not automatically independent origins. The same researcher’s earlier R02 role is disclosed. Both phases remain unlocated pending B01. The pilgrimage route is identified, but no crossing coordinate or gate geometry is certified by this audit.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the formal network-restoration phase and separate observed Tiptala trader passage. A network announcement and a named crossing observation are not additive independent closure events; potential programme overlap with Korala remains disclosed. P1 concerns seven immediate traditional points in six districts, with other openings staged and point-specific eligibility unresolved. P2 concerns thirty local Nepali traders entering China through Tiptala. Neither supports fourteen universally operational gates. P1 retains 25 May 2024 as a formal decision endpoint, not an observed operational reopening. P2 retains actual trader passage on 24 May, with the cached dated RSS extract establishing the year missing from the fresh extraction. Both onsets and continuity remain unknown; planned ten-day trading visits are not closure durations. The reported initial COVID explanation supports human disease control. It is not extended to every later delay or all traditional points for all intervening days. The ministry PDF fresh attempt timed out, leaving its old indexed extract at the same access level. Tiptala was freshly read; the Radio Nepal extract, Kathmandu Post and Xinhua passages were cached. Conflicting seven/fourteen counts are retained, and shared ministerial/RSS origins are not multiplied. P1 remains unlocated because its seven immediate gates are not individually identified. P2 matches OSM Tipta La node 990378815 at 27.8157775 / 87.7352531, with Tiptala aliases and membership in the NH02 approach way. Do not transfer this point to the whole network or outline the entire frontier.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the 12 October 2023 freight strike and reported same-day restoration. Workers’ body-return demand and subsequent assurance are documented. Import/export freight trucks are the affected cohort, with workers and unions imposing the stoppage. The BSF/body-return dispute does not make this a state-ordered passenger closure. Both dates remain 12 October. Jago’s eight-hour and Ajker’s nine-hour accounts conflict, while the English report is ongoing. Same-day restoration is retained with numeric duration and exact operational flags withheld. Rights/other-policy-grievance coding follows the stated demand to return the deceased driver’s body. No protectionist purpose is inferred. Jago was freshly read; the other two reports and two geographic sources were reused. Shared union/port spokespeople are not independent reconstruction, and the map source is not event evidence. The B01 approved approximate point exactly matches OSM node 7557117257 version 3: latitude 23.0379104, longitude 88.8839323. LPAI confirms crossing identity. Preserve freight-only scope and day-marker rule; this is not a barricade coordinate or passenger-denial claim.

Retain both quarantine decisions and all existing source/date/continuity/geographic limits. Accept the baseline challenger’s source-language, goods-attribution and Greek article-number refinements plus the additional limited source readings. The actual local-passholder endpoint is bounded November 13–14. Ordinary tourists and unrestricted freight are not established as reopened. Conflicting coarse onset accounts and pre-existing twice-yearly trading arrangements prevent a continuous four-year operational duration. Related network/crossing records may overlap; they are not counts of independent closure events. See the Dimensions relationship field.

followup_reviews.Research finding: The wartime outward-travel restriction and later age exemption are supported as national cohort policies. They do not establish closure of all Ukrainian frontier traffic. P1 concerns the general male-citizen 18–60 rule with exemptions. P2 concerns the remaining non-exempt 23–60 cohort after most 18–22-year-olds became eligible with documents; specified office-holder limits remain. The initial official notice is 24 February 2022. The amendment is effective on 28 August 2025, matching the implementation notice. The 11 September 2025 assessment supplies the later policy observation. Changing exemptions prevent a stable complete operational duration; neither phase receives one. The official initial notice connects the exit restriction to martial law. Security / Armed conflict remains source-attributed; mobilisation eligibility is a separate rule and is not substituted for exit permission. Official notices were read directly, the legislative text through an indexed extract after 403, and the dated Home Office assessment directly. The district notice’s 1030/registry 1031 discrepancy is already preserved. The Home Office wrapper’s 22 October 2026 update is not a new observation date. Both phases remain unlocated. A national outward cohort policy does not establish the operating status of every Ukraine–neighbour crossing or either side of a war-front boundary.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Six dated vehicle-access blockades are supported as separate phases, within one repeated protest parent. Planned additional blockades and general countrywide protest days do not create extra observed phases. Vehicles using the Leușeni–Albița access road in both directions. The reports identify tractor obstruction; a general pedestrian prohibition or all Moldova–Romania border closure is not established. P1 begins 12 February 2024 and ends near midnight, retaining a 12–13 February bound. P2–P6 separately cover 13, 14, 15, 22 and 23 February, each with same-day restoration reports and no whole-day duration. The gaps remain open rather than joined. Farmers sought economic relief and government engagement. The Jobs, services and livelihoods code is attributed to protestors, not framed as an official government closure rationale. The two IPN originals timed out but were read as indexed article text. NewsMaker and five broadcast articles were read directly. Broadcast restoration updates often relay Customs or Border Police; multiple outlets do not automatically create independent operational observations. All six phases are unlocated pending B01. The access obstruction must be represented at the reviewed road/crossing scope and cannot be expanded to the entire bilateral frontier.

followup_reviews.Researcher: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root/rounds_protocol
followup_reviews.Separate challenger: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root/verification_recovery, separate same-model context
followup_reviews.Research finding: The Greek customs strike caused observed vehicle restrictions at the two named Albania crossings, supporting the included parent. Cars and buses at Kakavija and Kapshtica. Pedestrian/passenger-without-bags and medical-emergency exceptions remain explicit. The report’s wider strike scope does not independently establish actual closure at Macedonia or Turkey crossings. P1 retains observed vehicle restriction on 30 May 2018 from the reported 07:00 onset, with no actual end. P2 preserves the overlapping planned 30–31 May 07:00–07:00 window. The two phases must not be added, and the planned finish is not observed reopening. The strike mechanism is established but the workers’ specific underlying demands are not. Retain Uncoded / Unresolved rationale rather than infer a socioeconomic demand from the fact of a strike alone. One BalkanWeb report contains named reporters’ observations at the two crossings and the announced union schedule. It is one reporting source, not independent confirmation of a completed 24-hour operational closure. Both phases remain unlocated pending B01. Neither a whole Greek border outline nor a coordinate binding is approved by this audit.

access_history.inspected: On 30 May the report describes cars and buses blocked from 07:00 at Kakavija and a similar situation at Kapshtica during the Greek strike. Pedestrians and emergency movement were exceptions. The stated 31 May 07:00 finish is scheduled, not an observed reopening.
access_history.limitation: A scheduled 24-hour window does not establish a complete operational duration. Specific workers’ demands were not established in this bounded round.

access_history.limitation: One reporting source supports the two observed crossing accounts and announced window; no independent actual-end confirmation was obtained.

access_history.limitation: Fresh reading confirms the existing operational/schedule distinction. It supplies no actual May 31 return or particular workers’ demands.

followup_reviews.Researcher: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root/rounds_protocol
followup_reviews.Separate challenger: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root/verification_recovery, separate same-model context
followup_reviews.Research finding: Two distinct Tompa–Kelebia interruptions are supported and remain included; the separate 8 February event is not joined to 6–7 February. P1 is road-crossing processing as described by police. P2 is only freight entering Hungary, while passenger movement in both directions and outbound freight continued. P1 starts 6 February 2020 at 16:00 and ends a few minutes after 7 February 07:00: about 15 hours, with a one-day calendar-date difference and unknown exact reopening minute. P2 is 8 February 10:30–11:16, 46 minutes, retained as same-day with no whole-day duration. Police cited safe/unobstructed crossing and security. Migrant presence is contextual; an additional unreported political motive is not inferred. The 24.hu report and MKFE notice share the same county-police origin. The 8 February primary police statement was directly read. These are source checks, not three independent witnesses. Both phases are currently unlocated. A narrower inbound freight gate on 8 February must not inherit an all-traffic geometry or a whole Hungary–Serbia frontier closure.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge

Apply the challenger’s medical-visa cohort, shared-reporting inference and unread-translation metadata refinements. source_index.Evidence by retrieval label:
[REC50-R06-S002] The report describes Skilpadshek as open for road freight on the morning of 9 July, with daytime operation only. A quoted C-BRTA statement attributes the recent suspension to unavailable port-health officials. Earlier disruption is described over eight weeks, without proving continuous closure or fixing the start of this particular suspension.
[REC50-R15-S105] The 9 July article reports freight operations resumed that morning, limited to 06:00–18:00. C-BRTA’s named spokesman attributes the suspension to absent port-health officials. Eight weeks of constrained service is not evidence of an eight-week continuous closure, and the exact onset of this suspension is not given.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the reported 15–16 July 2020 customs-service admission interruption and the observed reopening day. The phase concerns approaching/new cargo requiring South African customs facilities. Already admitted trucks continued processing with Mozambican help. Broad journalistic closure wording cannot erase that explicit exception or prove all passengers were stopped. The closure day 15 July and reported restoration day 16 July support a one-calendar-day difference and the existing day-precise complete/exact flags. The 13:00 SMS is announced timing; the 15:59 update is a status-post timestamp, not a first restored vehicle clock or exact elapsed-hour duration. Human disease control is supported by the SARS spokesman’s disinfection explanation after a positive staff test. The report’s varying staff labels do not alter the qualified generic official description. The decisive 16 July reopening update was freshly read. The initial report, reproduced SARS advisory and indexed UNECE entry were reused with original access limits. Reproduced notices and embedded social posts are not automatically independent observations. Original R06 authorship is disclosed. The accepted B02 row exactly matches the frozen guard and PIDA S10, -25.44311 / 31.98674. It locates the named crossing area while preserving approaching-cargo scope and unspecified direction, with a scoped interval. It is not the yard entrance or disinfection-room position.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain one campaign parent with four dated crossing/access observations. Reports name all four sites; this is not four independently counted campaign events. El Ceibo and Tecun Uman have unspecified road-movement scope on 7 October. El Carmen and La Mesilla have customs/freight evidence on 9 October. Do not infer every passenger cohort or a whole-frontier closure. All four first-closure and reopening bounds remain unknown. The 4 and 13 October road reports do not establish uninterrupted operation at the same barrier; numeric duration remains withheld. Power/regime coding reflects the sources’ attribution of campaign demands for prosecutors’ resignations. It is not an inferred personal rationale of every participant. One Prensa Libre customs account was freshly inspected; the other four exact passages were reused. Road summaries and shared official observations are not independent gate censuses. All four phases remain unlocated. The kilometre 565 road label and kilometre 657.5 customs location cannot be silently equated; no gate coordinate or national outline is added.

Integrated customs operations and redirected heavy freight are explicit. Exact direction-specific or other movement exceptions are not established. The 2025 government identity article concerns a different maintenance episode and supplies no 2021 traffic evidence. The 20 September–21 November 2021 dates support a 62-day policy lower bound, not a completed operational closure. Reopening remains unknown. Corinto’s hours through 15 January 2022 do not close the Agua Caliente interval; complete/exact operational flags stay zero. Administration and service operation reflects the authorities’ bridge installation and associated works explanation. No narrower rationale subcategory or protectionist purpose is invented. The November report was freshly read; the AGEXPORT webpage and circular were reread as one SAT-attributed institutional notice. The supplementary government article and six OSM identifiers concern geography, not eight additional historical confirmations. The accepted B02 row matches the frozen guard at 14.5313057 / -89.2830763. The saved XML makes this node common to CA-10 and the international-boundary watercourse; two Aduana controls are distinct nodes. Its station account dated the seventh describes a recently arrived ore train without an exact first-train day. A 6 February indexed commentary citing Xinhua on 4 February suggests earlier reporting but does not recover that operational date. This remains a policy-period phase.
source_phase.Qualification: Selected non-container rail imports were suspended from 28 November 2021, with permission for iron ore, coal and bagged goods in open wagons from 27 January 2022. This is a 60-day policy-date difference. An ore train was reported to have recently arrived by 7 February; its exact first arrival day remains unknown. EA029 concerns the separate China-to-Mongolia road-freight phase; its December dates are not rail endpoints. Container traffic and other commodity restoration dates are not generalised.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Contemporary reports establish intentional trucker obstruction at Cristo Redentor in January 2022, within the observation period; retain inclusion as a protest event distinct from health-control queues. The 20 January report concerns Chile-to-Argentina freight obstruction and the 26 January interview concerns Argentina-to-Chile entry. The record correctly describes differing observed directions without claiming continuous bidirectional closure. P1 retains exact 20 January onset evidence and 26 January last confirmation, no endpoint, held=1 and withheld_continuity. The 29 January protocol and 30 January general queue clearance do not provide a matched final protest endpoint. Numeric duration and both complete flags remain absent/zero. Policy and socioeconomic demands / Opposition to health policies remains supported by truckers’ stated objections to testing arrangements and effects on their work. It is their attributed demand, not the government’s health rationale or proof of every allegation. Both protest accounts were freshly read. The saved ministry and EFE/Emol passages were reread with fingerprints. EFE and its Emol republication are one origin, and official/association statements are not separate eyewitness observations. The single phase remains unlocated at the named road crossing and Argentine approach. No precise barricade coordinate, nationwide outline or continuous animation is justified.

The mirror is not independent of El Tribuno; the digest’s unnamed originating paper is not guessed from its URL. The bridge and immediate access remain unlocated; no blockade-point coordinate or continuous animation is inferred from the named place and overall protest dates.

Retain Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests for the seized-goods grievance, and Security / Public order and immediate safety for the mayor’s separate protection explanation. Neither validates alleged wrongdoing by customs. The broadcaster’s mayor interview, TAP-derived Tunisian reports and Al Wasat’s attributed Al Arab account have distinct or shared origins explicitly identified. Undated publication and prospective wording remain limits; repeated TAP accounts are not independent confirmations. Retain unlocated Dehiba–Wazen crossing and approach text, with null coordinates. events.consequences: No general economic effect is quantified in this round.
events.relationship: No matching Russian road-undertaking episode appears in the frozen northern inventory or R01–R21 additions. EU010 and the October 2023 car-import proposal concern different persons/vehicles and later dates.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Occurrence and inclusion remain supported for the April 2022 Russian road-undertaking prohibition, distinct from the later passenger-car rule and maritime port ban. Keep Russian-established road carriers as the restricted cohort. Pre-existing journeys, mail and authorised goods have exceptions. Supplies subsequently carried by a Norwegian operator do not establish return of Russian carriers. P1 retains formal onset 29 April 2022, confirmation through 6 July and a 68-calendar-day policy lower bound. The 7 May conditional grace is not a universal onset; the Norwegian-carrier workaround is not an endpoint. Retain the attributed sanctions rationale from the Norwegian government’s explicit statement about pressure and financing of the war. The policy notice was freshly read. E24 was reread from preserved full text and quotes ministry spokeswoman Ane Lunde, with NRK first reporting the solution; the common government origin is explicit. The documented Storskog route remains unlocated. No mainland perimeter or Svalbard border closure is inferred from the onward freight destination.

followup_reviews.Research finding: The included parent remains a selected-commodity rail restriction, with a formal steel phase and a separately evidenced cement return. It is not a total Kaliningrad blockade or the later Stasylos diversion. Passengers and non-sanctioned freight continued. Cement returned under essential-goods controls and quotas; luxury, military/dual-use and road limitations were not universally removed. P1 retains 17 June legal onset, 20 June confirmation and withheld duration. P2 retains unknown actual cement onset and an observed-return upper bound of 26 July. Neither 13 July guidance nor 22 July permission is an operational endpoint; first/second-train ambiguity remains. Retain official EU-sanctions implementation as the attributed rationale. Russian blockade descriptions remain interested-party characterisations, not an additional independently proven purpose. Interfax’s regional-spokesman account was freshly read. The decisive later BNS body was reread from cache after a fresh timeout, alongside earlier BNS/LRT and operator/ministerial text. BNS republications and LTG statements are not counted as independent news origins; the Commission body remains unavailable. Both phases remain unlocated. Propose removing the cement train’s Kena label from the steel phase and retaining a corridor-level, no-gate-established label. P2’s named Kena evidence is retained without coordinates.

followup_reviews.Research finding: The Chaman commercial interruption and July 2021 freight return remain included, separately from the August document dispute and returnee-only passenger exceptions. The observed return concerns freight into Afghanistan under Pakistani border authorities. Taliban control is context. Sunday returnees could pass while trade stayed closed. P1 retains unknown onset, trade confirmed closed on 25 July and scoped observed freight return on 26 July. Reuters reports over 100 trucks crossing. Earlier-this-month/month-long wording and earlier passenger openings do not establish a single continuous cargo duration. Retain Uncoded because neither fighting context nor change of control alone establishes the restricting authority’s stated purpose. The Reuters body was freshly read on Euronews; the separate NNI returnee report was reread from preserved text. Syndication is not a second Reuters origin, and the historic source records remain intact. The Chaman/Spin Boldak phase remains unlocated and evidence-only, with no new point or inferred entire-border geometry.

events.current_corrections: Formal Uganda–DRC ordinary-movement restriction commenced immediately in the signed May27,2026 notice and was reported current on May28. Cargo, response, humanitarian and security exceptions are explicit. The one-day minimum is a formal-policy date difference only; no expiry, physical onset or operational duration is inferred. The June15 certificate notice is unrelated to repeal. Ordinary-trader restrictions at Kasindi–Mpondwe are reported on May29 and July14; August18 documents a medical-referral permission, not general reopening. The October15 journalist visit found cargo crossing while ordinary markets and public transport remained suspended. These are dated observations, not a proved continuous May–October spell. Actual onset and reopening stay unknown; Ebola-free announcements and a June certificate notice are not endpoints.

events.rationale_phase_note: The signed Ugandan notice explicitly attributes the measure to limiting cross-border Ebola risk. The operational sources describe the same health restrictions, without proving a continuous spell or excluding every exception.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the Myawaddy–Mae Sot parent with two held, differently scoped phases. Cargo interruption and the temporary-document admission issue are documented, but source conflicts remain material. Keep Bridge II cargo separate from Bridge I temporary-pass/booklet passage. Passport exceptions, broader Myanmar-side closure accounts and the direction of permitted return traffic conflict; do not replace them with one all-persons or both-directions statement. Keep P1’s April 11–20 onset bounds and April 30 cargo return held without a numeric interval. Keep P2 as the April 21 document-cohort observation without matching restoration. Generic Bridge I reopening cannot end this precise cohort restriction. Retain Security / Armed conflict and military confrontation for the cargo phase only. Conflict context does not by itself resolve the imposing authority or assign an official motive to every Bridge I document refusal. RFA, Eleven, Mizzima, GNLM and CNI supply materially different accounts; GNLM, Mizzima and CNI are substantive indexed passages where direct access failed earlier. Their differing origins are disclosed, and apparent majority agreement is not used to erase contradictions. Retain separate unlocated Bridge I and Bridge II text with null coordinates. Side, document cohort and bridge identity stay separate; a later nine-month shutdown is not backdated into the 2024 phase.

The reported commercial return is not silently treated as a separately observed passenger restoration. Retain same-day evidence and withhold elapsed duration. El Diario’s 10:00 onset, NotiGAPE’s earlier report time and Hora Cero’s 14:30 commercial return are not forced into an exact hours calculation. A proposed partial release is not an actual endpoint. Retain Policy and socioeconomic demands / Jobs, services and livelihoods, based on attributed sorghum compensation and agricultural-support demands. The protest’s use of a trade bridge does not alone supply a protectionist motive. Contemporary local and national reports support occurrence and same-day return, but clock details and cohort precision differ. NotiGAPE remains an inspected indexed passage after its earlier direct-access failure; no presumed independence of every repeated event claim. Retain unlocated Mexican access to Pharr–Reynosa and null coordinates. The separate domestic highway actions and other international bridges are not added to this phase.

events.enforcement: Trade resumed on 23 May morning after a five-day halt, with goods trucks at both port areas. The immigration OC said ordinary Bangladeshi travellers had faced a separate three-day ban beginning 17 May at 18:00, with patient and Indian-passport exceptions.

That inconsistent report establishes later open status, not a safe first-return date or six-day continuous ban. Medical/emergency travellers and returning Indians were exceptions; freight’s May 23 endpoint is not transferred.
